flamenco-rasgueo.title: Flamenco: rasgueo (strumming)
flamenco-rasgueo.description: The flamenco strumming hand, step by step: from rumba to bulerías, through tangos, sevillanas and the 12-beat compás of soleá. New symbol: ⇊ = rasgueado (your fingers unfold one after the other).

flamenco-r01-rumba-noires.title: Rumba: four solid beats
flamenco-r01-rumba-noires.description: Your first meeting with the flamenco band: cajón, palmas and bass. Just strum the four beats on a single chord (Am), to get used to the palmas clapping off the beat, between your strums.
flamenco-r01-rumba-noires.goal: Four steady strums per bar, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Tap your foot on every beat: your strum lands with your foot, the palmas land in between.
Listen to the low cajón hit on 1 and 3: it's your most reliable landmark.
Strum with your index finger flicking open downward (the nail hits the strings): that's already a flamenco gesture.

flamenco-r02-golpe.title: The muted hit on 2 and 4
flamenco-r02-golpe.description: In rumba, the guitar imitates the cajón: a strum on 1 and 3, a muted, percussive hit on 2 and 4, together with the cajón slap. That "chak" is where all the energy comes from.
flamenco-r02-golpe.goal: Your ✕ right with the cajón slap, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: To mute: let your palm (the edge of your hand) drop onto the strings as you strum. You hear "chak", no notes.
Say "boom CHAK boom CHAK" while you play.
Mute the palmas (click "palmas") to hear only the cajón, then bring them back.

flamenco-r03-rumba-base.title: The rumba rhythm
flamenco-r03-rumba-base.description: The most famous rumba pattern: down, chuck-up, up, chuck-up. Your hand swings non-stop in eighth notes and only touches the strings on some steps. Still on Am, so you can focus on your strumming hand.
flamenco-r03-rumba-base.goal: The pattern without stopping your hand, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Your hand never stops: down on the beats, up on the "&"s, even when it doesn't touch the strings.
Say "BOOM . CHAK-a . a CHAK-a": the "a"s are the upstrokes.
The ✕s land on 2 and 4, just like in the previous exercise: hold on to that.
If you stumble, first play it without the ✕s (replace them with a normal down).

flamenco-r04-rumba-cadence.title: Rumba over the Andalusian cadence
flamenco-r04-rumba-cadence.description: The Andalusian cadence (Am, G, F, E7) is the progression that instantly "sounds flamenco": it walks down to a tense E7. Same rumba pattern, one chord per bar.
flamenco-r04-rumba-cadence.goal: Changes on time without breaking the pattern, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Change chords during the last upstroke of the bar: it's a light stroke and forgives small slips.
Am → G → F → E7: the bass walks down A, G, F, E. Listen to it and sing it.
Get the E7 (1202) ready early: keep your index finger on fret 1 of the G string.

flamenco-r05-tangos-premier-temps.title: Tangos: the guitar fills beat 1
flamenco-r05-tangos-premier-temps.description: In tangos, the palmas stay silent on beat 1 and clap 2, 3, 4. Your guitar plays loud on 1, then softer on the other beats: you share the work with the palmas.
flamenco-r05-tangos-premier-temps.goal: A strong 1 in the palmas' silence, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Uppercase = loud, lowercase = soft: only one big strum per bar, on 1.
Listen to the "hole" in the palmas: your 1 must land right in it.
Count "ONE two three four" out loud, almost shouting the ONE.

flamenco-r06-rasgueado.title: The fan rasgueado
flamenco-r06-rasgueado.description: The king of flamenco gestures: instead of a single downstroke, your fingers unfold one after the other (pinky, ring, middle, index) to make a "trrrra". Here it replaces the big strum on beat 1 of the tangos.
flamenco-r06-rasgueado.goal: A clean rasgueado that ends right on the beat, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Close your fist gently, thumb resting on the G string. Then open your fingers one by one, starting with the pinky, like a fan.
Practise it first without the band, slowly: four well-separated "clicks", then closer and closer together.
The last finger (the index) is the loudest: it's the one that lands on the beat.
The motion comes from the fingers, not the wrist: your hand stays almost still.

flamenco-r07-tangos-golpe.title: Tangos: rasgueado and golpe
flamenco-r07-tangos-golpe.description: A real tangos accompaniment: rasgueado on 1, small down-up strokes, and a muted hit (the "golpe") on 3, with the cajón slap. Over the Andalusian cadence you already know.
flamenco-r07-tangos-golpe.goal: The full pattern over the 4 chords, 2 loops at 105 bpm.
tips: Break it down: "TRRRA . ti-ta CHAK . ti-ta".
On guitar, the flamenco golpe is a tap on the top with the ring finger; on ukulele, a palm mute does the job nicely.
If the rasgueado makes you late, replace it with a simple D while you settle the pattern.

flamenco-r08-tangos-por-arriba.title: Tangos "por arriba": E, F, G, F
flamenco-r08-tangos-por-arriba.description: Flamenco loves the E mode (Phrygian mode): the home chord is E (here E7), and the F just above gives that typical Arabic-Andalusian colour. Same pattern as before, new progression, and the guide fades after 2 loops.
flamenco-r08-tangos-por-arriba.goal: The progression by heart, guide off, 2 loops at 110 bpm.
tips: E7 → F: only your fingers move, keep your hand close to the neck.
Listen to the E → F half step in the bass: it's THE sound of flamenco.
The progression returns to E7 every time round: that's "home", you always come back to it.

flamenco-r09-sevillanas-trois.title: Sevillanas: counting in 3
flamenco-r09-sevillanas-trois.description: New time signature: sevillanas are in 3. Three downstrokes per bar, the first one louder, and one chord per bar. The castanets roll on beat 1: that's your landmark.
flamenco-r09-sevillanas-trois.goal: A clearly marked 1, 2 loops at 130 bpm.
tips: Count "ONE two three, ONE two three": like a waltz, but with more drive.
The castanet roll always announces beat 1.
Am ↔ E7: practise this change without strumming before you start.

flamenco-r10-sevillanas-rasgueado.title: Sevillanas: rasgueado on 1
flamenco-r10-sevillanas-rasgueado.description: The rasgueado arrives on beat 1 of the sevillanas, followed by a down on 2 and a down-up on 3. The progression is 8 bars long, like a phrase of the dance: Am-E7 twice, then the Andalusian cadence.
flamenco-r10-sevillanas-rasgueado.goal: All 8 bars without stopping, 2 loops at 135 bpm.
tips: "TRRRA . ta . ta-ti": the rasgueado fills the whole of beat 1.
The little upstroke at the end of the bar is the perfect moment to change chords.
Two-thirds of the way through come G then F: watch the "next" box so you're not caught out.

flamenco-r11-solea-accents.title: Soleá: accents only
flamenco-r11-solea-accents.description: The 12-beat compás! To discover it, strum only on the accents: 3, 6, 8, 10 and 12 (the circled dots). In between, count silently. The chord moves to F on beat 7 and back to E7 on beat 10.
flamenco-r11-solea-accents.goal: All 5 accents in place, 2 loops at 110 bpm.
tips: Count out loud: "one two THREE four five SIX seven EIGHT nine TEN eleven TWELVE".
Feel the groups: 1-2-3, 4-5-6, then 7-8, 9-10, 11-12. Two groups of three, three groups of two.
The change to F comes on 7, a beat you don't play: make the most of it.
The metronome click is higher-pitched on the accents.

flamenco-r12-solea-tous-les-temps.title: Soleá: every beat, strong accents
flamenco-r12-solea-tous-les-temps.description: Now you play all 12 beats: light strums on the weak beats, strong strums on the accents. The difference in volume is what draws the compás: if everything is at the same level, the soleá disappears.
flamenco-r12-solea-tous-les-temps.goal: A real loud/soft difference, 2 loops at 115 bpm.
tips: Light strums: just your index finger, close to the strings. Strong strums: all your fingers, with a bit more swing.
Not faster on the accents: only louder.
Listen to the bright palmas: they clap exactly on your accents.

flamenco-r13-solea-rasgueados.title: Soleá: rasgueados on the accents
flamenco-r13-solea-rasgueados.description: Accents 3, 6 and 10 become rasgueados, 8 stays a clean strum, and 12 ends with a golpe (muted hit) that closes the compás. This is what a soleá accompaniment sounds like.
flamenco-r13-solea-rasgueados.goal: The full compás without losing your place, 2 loops at 120 bpm.
tips: The rasgueado must end ON the accent: start the motion a tiny bit early.
The golpe on 12 closes the phrase, like a full stop at the end of a sentence.
If you get lost, don't panic: wait for the next 1 while counting, and start again.
Use "🐢 Too fast!" as soon as the rasgueados get messy.

flamenco-r14-alegrias.title: Alegrías: the compás in major
flamenco-r14-alegrias.description: The same 12-beat compás, but in A major and more joyful. Over two compases: A on 1-2, then E7 from accent 3; the next compás stays on E7 and returns to A on accent 10. Chords change on the accents: that's the flamenco rule.
flamenco-r14-alegrias.goal: Both changes right on 3 and on 10, 2 loops at 130 bpm.
tips: First find the two changes without strumming: left hand only, counting.
A (2100) → E7 (1202): your index finger slides from the C string to the G string.
The palmas clap off the beat: don't get dragged along, your foot stays on the beats.

flamenco-r15-bulerias.title: Bulerías: the compás that flies
flamenco-r15-bulerias.description: The soleá pattern (rasgueados on 3, 6, 10, golpe on 12) at bulería tempo. At this speed, you no longer count the 12 beats: you feel the accents. The guide fades after 2 loops. This is the culmination of the path.
flamenco-r15-bulerias.goal: Hold 2 loops at 170 bpm, guide off.
tips: Fast = small motions: your fingers stay right next to the strings.
Count only the accents: "THREE . . SIX . EIGHT . TEN . TWELVE".
The palmas and cajón play around the accents: listen to them as a conversation, not a metronome.
Your record is saved: a few more bpm each session.
